page: Amazon Web Services x8i.48xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. The system incorporates an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked up to 3.9 GHz, delivering 96 physical cores and 192 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading. The processor architecture includes a substantial cache layout comprising 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a combined 480 MB L3 cache pool. Advanced instruction extensions are present, including AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8 for matrix operations. The instance is provisioned with 3072.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, delivering 16.0 GB of memory per core. Local direct-attached storage is not present, requiring remote EBS storage configurations. Network performance features a baseline throughput of 75 Gbps, and no discrete GPUs are bundled.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded scaling and memory throughput. The server achieves top-tier results in multi-core metrics, including a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 207532.01, a Geekbench multi-core score of 21793.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 144271.62. Memory bandwidth tests reach 515.9 GB/sec for uncached 256MB reads and 222.15 GB/sec for 256MB writes. Highly parallelized operations reflect this compute density, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 1160.84 GB/sec and Redis SET performance reaching 274.54 million operations per second. Hardware matrix extensions also contribute to strong LLM prompt processing speeds, reaching 335.49 tokens per second on 7B parameter models and 44.25 tokens per second on 70B models.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the x8i.48xlarge presents a consolidated footprint for enterprise-scale workloads requiring high RAM-to-vCPU ratios. While single-threaded performance registers in the average to strong ranges, multi-core throughput and raw memory density provide strong operational efficiency for centralized, monolithic in-memory datasets. Tradeoffs include the total absence of integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures, and the lack of dedicated GPU hardware for accelerating training workloads. Workload fit includes in-memory databases such as Redis and SAP HANA, large-scale data analytics, in-memory caching systems, complex multi-threaded compilations, and enterprise-grade ETL pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services x8i.48xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running up to 3.9 GHz. It features 96 physical cores, 192 dedicated vCPUs, and 480 MB of L3 cache, backed by 3072.0 GB of high-frequency 7 GHz DDR5 memory at a ratio of 16.0 GB per core. The instance provides 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without local disk storage or discrete GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded processing, leading results in database operations, and high uncached memory read bandwidth of 515.9 GB/sec. Given its compute consolidation and massive RAM capacity, the instance is targeted at large-scale in-memory databases, Redis deployments, enterprise analytics engines, and intensive multi-threaded compilation tasks.
